families.title: Bayesian and Markov networks
families.intro: Networks against the tools people use for them: Ace 3.0, which compiles a network into an arithmetic circuit, and Merlin 1.7.0's bucket-tree elimination (`-a bte`, and `-t PR` for the partition function), and the other exact network tools: pyAgrum (junction tree), pgmpy (variable elimination), libDAI (junction tree) and TensorInference.jl (tensor network contraction; of its two contraction orders, `treesa` and `greedy`, the faster is shown). On the standard suite's networks ProbLog, PITA and aspmc ran too. tddlog reads a network as a ProbLog program, one annotated disjunction per row of a table.

cards.title: Standard suite: networks
paras: **Against Ace:** both answer all 34. On the 34 both answer, tddlog is faster on all 34, by a median of 70 times (3.95 s against 107.9 in all).

**Against Merlin:** both answer all 34. Of the 34 both answer, both take under 0.1 s on 24; on the other 10, tddlog is faster on 8 (by a median of 6.5 times) and slower on 2 (by a median of 4.1 times), 3.56 s against 64.1 in all. tddlog is slower on bn_pathfinder_ev (0.30 s against Merlin's 0.07) and bn_pathfinder (0.31 s against Merlin's 0.08).

**Against pyAgrum:** both answer all 34. On the 34 both answer, tddlog is faster on 32 (by a median of 9.2 times) and slower on 2 (by a median of 1.7 times), 3.95 s against 99.3 in all. tddlog is slower on bn_pathfinder_ev (0.30 s against pyAgrum's 0.17) and bn_pathfinder (0.31 s against pyAgrum's 0.20).

**Against pgmpy:** tddlog answers all 34 and pgmpy 30. On the 30 both answer, tddlog is faster on all 30, by a median of 108 times (1.22 s against 108.2 in all). tddlog alone answers bn_link_ev, bn_link, bn_munin_ev and bn_munin.

suites.title: Standard suite: networks
suites.about: 34 Bayesian networks of the bnlearn repository, with and without evidence, one annotated disjunction per row of a table, every leaf queried; 300 s a run.

suites.title: Ace's networks
suites.about: The 46 networks of Ace's benchmarks (Chavira and Darwiche), each with one of the archive's evidence sets; 600 s a run.

suites.title: Large networks
suites.about: barley, diabetes, mildew and munin1 to munin4, with and without evidence, the large networks of the flip-hoisting evaluation (Cheng et al., 2021); 600 s a run.

suites.title: UAI 2022: marginals
suites.about: The 120 Markov and Bayesian networks of the UAI 2022 competition's MAR tuning set, each with its evidence; every marginal given the evidence; 300 s a run.

suites.title: UAI 2022: partition function, final set
suites.about: The 197 networks of the UAI 2022 competition's final PR set: tddlog prints the probability of the evidence alone (`--evidence-probability --no-queries`) and Merlin and the other network tools run their partition function tasks; 300 s a run.

suites.title: UAI 2022: partition function, tuning set
suites.about: The 121 networks of the UAI 2022 competition's PR tuning set: tddlog prints the probability of the evidence alone (`--evidence-probability --no-queries`) and Merlin and the other network tools run their partition function tasks; 300 s a run.

suites.title: UAI 2022: partition function of the MAR set
suites.about: The 120 networks of the UAI 2022 competition's MAR tuning set: tddlog prints the probability of the evidence alone (`--evidence-probability --no-queries`) and Merlin and the other network tools run their partition function tasks; 300 s a run.

setup: Three jobs on two lab machines (36 and 20 physical cores, 503 GB each), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20: every system of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes; Ace in 12 wide lanes of 88 GB, half of it its Java heap. The systems of an instance run in the same lanes, so their times compare.
Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced.

tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically (tididi e4d60911, goatd e237c1a). Ace 3.0, Merlin 1.7.0, pyAgrum 3.2.1, pgmpy 1.1.2, libDAI 0.3.2, TensorInference.jl, ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD.

Every answer of tddlog's, and of each other system, is compared with a reference: the clique tree (`scripts/bn_exact.py`), Ace or Merlin. The largest absolute differences: 6.3e-15 on Ace's networks, 4.9e-11 on the large networks, 9.1e-14 on the 111 UAI networks the clique tree answers (the other six agree with Merlin's six printed digits); no other system answers Grids_16, Grids_17 and Grids_18. For the partition function tddlog's log10 Z agrees with every other exact answer there is: Merlin's, the clique tree's, or a weighted model count of the network. The other network tools' answers against the same references: pyAgrum 180 marginal runs to 2.0e-7 and 108 partition functions to 5.6e-9 in log10; pgmpy 102 marginal runs to 1.2e-10 and 103 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10; libDAI 190 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 120 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10; TensorInference.jl 281 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 176 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10 (the tools print six digits, as Merlin does).

families.title: Probabilistic logic programs
families.intro: Programs in ProbLog's language against ProbLog 2.3.0 (d-DNNF, SDD and forward SDD compilation), PITA's BDDs and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD, and, on TPC-H, ProvSQL 1.13.0, a PostgreSQL extension that tracks provenance and picks its method for the probability. Scallop's top-k proofs ran too; they are approximate, so their times are in the tables of docs/benchmarks.md and not here.

setup: Three jobs on two lab machines (36 and 20 physical cores, 503 GB each), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20: every system of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes; Ace in 12 wide lanes of 88 GB, half of it its Java heap. The systems of an instance run in the same lanes, so their times compare.
Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced.
tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically (tididi e4d60911, goatd e237c1a). ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD; ProvSQL 1.13.0 on PostgreSQL 16.4.

Every answer of tddlog's is compared with a reference: ProbLog's, or an exact solver written for the suite (`scripts/lit_exact.py`, `tpch_exact.py`, `reliability_exact.py`). The largest absolute differences: 4.9e-9 on the standard suite (ProbLog prints eight digits), 2.7e-13 on the literature suite, 1.0e-14 on TPC-H, 3.4e-12 on Biomine; ProvSQL's answers differ from the reference's by at most 1.0e-12 on TPC-H. The random graphs and grids no exact system finishes agree with estimates from sampled graphs (`scripts/sample_paths.py`).
